headline: Zendesk's AI Agents Lost Chats in Europe for Nearly Five Days, per its own incident report
summary: Zendesk's AI Agents Advanced product experienced a five-day outage in Europe, causing customer and agent messages to be delayed or lost. The company's incident report cites a capacity problem as the cause.
details: Zendesk's AI Agents Advanced product in Europe suffered a major incident from October 16 to 21, causing customer and agent messages to be delayed or entirely missing. This five-day disruption also impacted conversation histories and analytics for EU customers.

According to Zendesk's own incident report, a recovery attempt had to be paused to prevent further slowdowns in other parts of the service. The company identified a capacity problem as the root cause of the outage.
Zendesk has since confirmed that all affected messages have been restored. The incident highlights the challenges of maintaining robust infrastructure for AI-powered customer service solutions.

topic: Hacktoberfest projects showcase local AI and open-source security
headline_marked: [[Team builds local AI decision intelligence CLI]] at overnight Hacktoberfest hackathon
headline: Team builds local AI decision intelligence CLI at overnight Hacktoberfest hackathon
summary: IssueFlowP6 is a privacy-first CLI tool that uses a local Qwen 2.5 model via Ollama to extract and verify architectural decisions from developer chat logs, preventing AI hallucinations and proprietary code leaks.
details: An overnight Hacktoberfest hackathon challenged a team to solve a common engineering problem: lost context in architectural decisions. Critical choices made in chat threads are often forgotten, and standard cloud LLMs risk hallucinating facts or leaking proprietary code when summarizing them.

To address this, the team built IssueFlowP6, a completely offline Decision Intelligence CLI. This privacy-first tool extracts decisions locally and rigorously fact-checks them. It uses a local Qwen 2.5 model via Ollama to process raw developer chat logs.

The author focused on the extraction architecture, writing Python logic to feed chat logs into Qwen 2.5 and force a strict JSON schema output. This included the final decision, rejected alternatives, and verbatim supporting quotes. A mid-hackathon Git panic taught a valuable lesson on hard resets and branch isolation.

While the extraction was being built, another team member developed a deterministic verification engine to catch AI hallucinations. A third member wrapped all scripts into a clean command-line interface. The integrated pipeline successfully parsed text, intercepted two hallucinated quotes, and produced a perfectly verified JSON file.

The project, built from scratch in a single night, resulted in a fully functional, privacy-first local AI tool. This achievement was a significant win for the team, regardless of the final judging in the Hacktoberfest blog challenge.
